PhotoSlop · free, in your browser

A free Photoshop alternative in your browser

If you need layers, masks and PSD files but not a subscription or an install, PhotoSlop opens in a browser tab. It uses familiar tool names and shortcuts, and your files stay on your computer.

Open PhotoSlop

Watch the PhotoSlop tutorial: a free photo editor in the browser
On YouTube, about two minutes.

How to do it

  1. Open PhotoSlop and choose File > New… or File > Open… (PSD, ORA, TIFF, PNG, JPG, WebP and more).
  2. Work in layers: masks, clipping, 17 blend modes and layer styles such as Drop Shadow and Stroke.
  3. Use the tools you know: Move, Marquee, Lasso, Magic Wand, Brush, Clone Stamp, Healing Brush, Gradient, Type and Crop.
  4. Adjust with Levels, Curves, Hue/Saturation and more, and add filters from the Filter menu.
  5. Save a layered PSD, or export PNG, JPEG or WebP.

What it does not have yet: adjustment layers, content-aware fill, a pen tool for paths, RAW files and animation. It is a good fit for layered edits, retouching, compositing and PSD handoffs.

Your files stay on this device: PhotoSlop runs in your browser, with no upload, no account and no watermark.

Questions

Is PhotoSlop really free?

Yes. There is no plan, no account and no watermark on what you export.

Can I open and save PSD files?

Yes. PhotoSlop opens PSDs with their layers and masks, and saves layered 8-bit RGB PSDs. Groups are flattened and Photoshop text opens as pixels.

Does it work offline?

Yes. File > Download PhotoSlop for offline use (.html) saves a copy of the editor as one file that you can open without a connection.

Is PhotoSlop made by Adobe?

Slopographic is not affiliated with Adobe. Photoshop is a trademark of its owner, and the name is used here only to say what this app can stand in for.
